reason: The text describes Yahweh setting protective boundaries around Mount Sinai and Moses acknowledging these divinely ordained restrictions. When Moses states 'the people cannot go up to Mount Sinai because you have testified to us,' he is conveying a fact about Yahweh's protective commands, not expressing blame. The passage focuses on warnings and instructions to keep the people safe from a holy, dangerous place. There is no indication of the people or their leaders blaming Yahweh or leadership for putting them at risk; instead, the narrative presents obedience to safety regulations.
